body.p: After installation, you can start as follows:

li.p: Windows hosts. In the Programs menu, click the item in the VirtualBox group. On some Windows platforms, you can also enter VirtualBox in the search box of the Start menu.
macOS hosts. In the Finder, double-click the VirtualBox item in the Applications folder. You may want to drag this item onto your Dock.

Linux or Oracle Solaris hosts. Depending on your desktop environment, an item may have been placed in either the System or System Tools group of your Applications menu. Alternatively, you can enter VirtualBox in a terminal window.

body.p: When you start , the interface is shown. See .
The main toolbar, machine selection, and rounded details cards use the application color theme. Selected machines use the theme's highlight and matching text colors in both light and dark modes.

The About dialog shows the product version, contact details, build information, and credits on one scrollable page. Use Copy Build Information to copy the product and platform versions, build type, and source revision for a support request.
Dialogs center their window frame within the visible part of the parent window or the available screen area.

section.title: Android Phones in Navebox
section.p: Choose File, then Android Phones, to create and manage Android virtual phones with a separately installed Android SDK. Install Android Emulator, Platform-Tools, Command-Line Tools and a stable phone image matching the host CPU (API 26 or newer) using the standalone SDK tools or Android Studio's SDK Manager. Android Studio is optional. Open SDK Settings, select the SDK and a compatible Java home in the phone manager, click Apply SDK, then Check Acceleration, then Done.
SDK Settings replaces the phone pages while it is open. Applying an SDK keeps setup open for the acceleration check. Click Done to return to the phone pages.

On Create Phone, choose a name, image, memory, CPUs, storage and device profile. Vary for testing selects a supported hardware profile and display at creation. Phones with the same image can share the Android build fingerprint. After creation, the new phone is selected on Phones; click Start. The emulator opens in its own window. When its status is Ready, use Install APK or the navigation actions under More. More, then Cold Boot, skips loading a snapshot without deleting phone data. If GPU Auto fails, Cold Boot with Software Graphics uses a software renderer for the session on supported SDK versions. Stop shuts down the selected emulator.

Phone data is stored in a separate Phones directory under the application's local data directory. Android Studio's device catalog is not modified. Closing Navebox leaves the phones running; reopen the phone manager to discover them again. Use More, then Open Log, to inspect a startup failure. Navebox does not install SDK packages, accept SDK licenses, or change host virtualization settings. APK compatibility depends on the selected Android image and its supported CPU ABI.
